lessons.title: The Rich Don't Work for Money
lessons.key_idea: Through young Robert's low-paid job at rich dad's store, the book shows how fear and desire keep people chasing paychecks, and why learning to make money work for you is the way out of the rat race.

lessons.title: Buy Assets, Not Liabilities
lessons.key_idea: Wealth comes from building a column of assets that put money in your pocket, like businesses and rental property, rather than buying liabilities, including a home you live in, which take money out.

lessons.title: Mind Your Own Business
lessons.key_idea: Your profession is not your business, so keep your day job while steadily building your own column of assets, much as McDonald's grew rich from the land under its restaurants and not only from selling burgers.

That is below the 18px minimum, and the 'ASSETS' label is crowded against the bottom of the bin. (fix: Raise both labels to at least 20px. Move the 'ASSETS' label about 10px further below the bin so it has clear spacing.)

lessons.title: Taxes and the Power of Corporations
lessons.key_idea: Understanding tax law and using corporations lets the rich earn, spend, and then pay tax on what remains, while employees are taxed before they ever see their pay.

lessons.title: Financial Intelligence Creates Opportunity
lessons.key_idea: Financial knowledge lets you see deals others miss and create your own luck, such as buying property cheaply when a market crashes and everyone else is afraid.

lessons.title: Work to Learn, Not to Earn
lessons.key_idea: Choose jobs for the skills they teach, especially selling, communication and managing systems, because many people can cook a better burger than McDonald's but few can build the business behind it.

lessons.title: Overcoming the Obstacles Within
lessons.key_idea: Cynicism, laziness, bad habits and arrogance hold people back, and simple shifts like paying yourself first and asking how you can afford something help you break through them.

lessons.title: Getting Started on Your Path
lessons.key_idea: Turning these lessons into wealth starts with a strong personal reason, a daily choice to spend time and money on learning and assets, and small first steps taken now.

plan.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
plan.author: Robert T. Kiyosaki (with Sharon Lechter)
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's core lessons, framing and main stories in detail, though I avoid fine specifics I can't verify.
plan.one_liner: Two fathers, two money mindsets, and why working harder alone rarely makes anyone rich.
plan.summary: Robert Kiyosaki tells the story of growing up in Hawaii with two father figures. His own father was highly educated and held a respected government job, yet he struggled with money all his life. His best friend's father left school early but built real wealth through businesses and property. Through the lessons of this rich dad, Kiyosaki argues that schools teach people to work for money but rarely teach how money actually works. He urges readers to learn the difference between assets, which put money in your pocket, and liabilities, which take money out. He warns that fear and desire keep people trapped in a cycle of earning and spending that he calls the rat race. His answer is financial literacy, steadily building assets, and choosing work for what it teaches rather than just the paycheck.
